content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail: Start digital

The current state of digital commerce is built on a fragile foundation – platforms like PayPal and Stripe can freeze or reject your funds at any time, leaving you with no way to access your money. This problem is not unique to any one country or region – it's a global issue that affects creators in many parts of the world. By building a sovereign digital commerce stack, you can avoid this problem altogether and maintain full control over your online store and payment processing.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you start building your sovereign digital commerce stack, you need to choose the right tools and infrastructure. You'll need a hosting platform like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, a backend logic tool like Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, an order storage solution like Supabase or Google Sheets, and a file delivery system like Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. You'll also need a payment processing tool like NOWPayments, which charges a fee of just 0.5% on every sale.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

With your tools and infrastructure in place, it's time to set up your payment and delivery pipeline. This involves connecting your NOWPayments account to your chosen payment method, setting up automatic on-chain crypto payment verification, and configuring your file delivery system to send products to customers instantly. By doing this, you can ensure that your customers receive their products quickly and easily, while you receive your payments in full.
You can save up to $921 per month by switching from Gumroad to NOWPayments.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, it's time to go live and process your first transaction. This involves deploying your sovereign digital commerce stack, loading your products into the system, and setting up automatic webhook notifications to alert you to new transactions. By following these steps, you can ensure that your online store is up and running and ready to accept payments from customers.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

As your online store grows and more customers start to buy from you, you'll need to scale your infrastructure to keep up with demand. This involves monitoring your system for performance issues, adjusting your payment processing settings as needed, and configuring your file delivery system to handle increased traffic. By doing this, you can ensure that your online store remains fast and reliable, even as it grows and expands.
